source.section: IT 1040 lines 1 to 8a (bundle PDF p.1); booklet PDF p.16 lines 1 to 4; PDF p.17 line 4 exemption table and line 8a; PDF p.18 bracket table; PDF p.5 rounding; Schedule of Adjustments line 16 (PDF p.20; bundle PDF p.3); Senior Citizens page 'Social Security Benefits'; MAGI PDF p.8; MAGI less exemptions worksheet PDF p.40; Schedule of Credits line 2 (PDF p.28; Table 2 PDF p.44; bundle PDF p.7); Department FAQ 2; Schedule of Credits line 4 (PDF p.28; bundle PDF p.7); Department FAQ 2

worked: Federal AGI = private pension person 0 44,000.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 = 78,000.00. Federal taxable income = 78,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 60,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored; Ohio starts from federal AGI). IT 1040 line 1 federal AGI 78,000.00. Schedule of Adjustments additions: line 1 non-Ohio state or local interest 0.00; line 12 total 0.00; line 2a 0.00. Deductions: line 16 taxable Social Security 34,000.00; line 47 total 34,000.00; line 2b 34,000.00. Line 3 Ohio AGI = 78,000.00 + 0.00 - 34,000.00 = 44,000.00. Line 4: MAGI is line 3 with no business income deduction, 44,000.00, in the band 40,001 to 80,000: 2,150.00 each; 1 exemption x 2,150.00 = 2,150.00. Line 5 = 44,000.00 - 2,150.00 = 41,850.00. Line 6 taxable business income 0.00. Line 7 = 41,850.00. Line 8a tax: 41,850.00 is in the 26,050 to 100,000 band: 342.00 plus 2.750% of (41,850.00 - 26,050.00 = 15,800.00) = 342.00 + 434.50 = 776.50. Schedule of Credits line 1 = 776.50. MAGI less exemptions (worksheet PDF p.40) = 44,000.00 - 2,150.00 = 41,850.00 (equal to line 7 without business income), under 100,000.00. Line 2 retirement income credit: covered retirement income 44,000.00; 200.00 (Table 2 at 8,001 or more: 200). Line 4 senior citizen credit: taxpayer is 65 or older at the end of the year; 50.00 per return. Line 10 credits = 200.00 + 50.00 = 250.00. Line 11 = 776.50 - 250.00 = 526.50. State income tax 526.50. The form works in whole dollars ('Round all figures to the nearest dollar', PDF p.5): line 8a would be 777; expected keeps the formula result. 'Ohio does not tax Social Security benefits.' The taxable amount comes off on line 16 and does not count as retirement income.
